newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu poised to close Hebron deal with PLO.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu poised to close Hebron deal with PLO.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian officials said on Monday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was poised to hand over the occupied West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas said the long-elusive deal to transfer 80 percent of Hebron would probably be signed at a summit on Tuesday between Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Netanyahu, the Likud party leader elected in May.

"We expect to conclude today all the subjects...After signing, in a very short time redeployment will take place. I came here to bridge the gaps," Israel's Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told reporters when he joined talks in Jerusalem.
PLO negotiator Mohammad Dahlan said a troop redeployment would take place within a week.

Opposed to swapping occupied land for peace, the 47-year-old Netanyahu ran an election campaign against the self-rule accords that Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres, his Nobel prize-winning predecessors, signed with the PLO starting in 1993.
But also promising to uphold existing peace deals, Netanyahu managed to oust Peres, albeit by fewer than 30,000 votes.

Hebron, long a flashpoint of violence between Arabs and Jews, is the last of seven West Bank towns scheduled for self-rule under an agreement signed in 1995. It was due to have been given self-rule nine months ago.

But security concerns held up the handover. Peres delayed it over a wave of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel that killed 59 people. Then talks got stuck on Netanyahu's demands for better protection for the 400 Jews in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs. Arafat also put forward demands.

Many of Netanyahu's right-wing followers, including Jewish settlers, view the West Bank as the biblical birthright of Jews -- the Land of Israel promised them by God. Many view Arafat as a terrorist bent on Israel's destruction.

"The problem of Hebron is very serious. But it's not only the problem of Hebron. Hebron is only the first break in the dike. When it's broken it's a flood that might endanger all the country," said Hebron settlers spokesman Noam Arnon.

U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross, who pushed and pulled the sides together on orders from President Bill Clinton, was due back in the Middle East on Monday, flying in from Washington to mediate any last-minute snags.

Under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, Netanyahu stayed in the negotiations while emphasising that 20 percent of the town, including Hebron's Jews and the tomb of the biblical patriarch Abraham, would remain under Israeli control.

Underscoring tensions in Hebron, Israeli troops arrested several Palestinian construction workers on Monday after Jewish settlers complained they were doing work close to a Jewish enclave in the town, Palestinian witnesses said.

Erekat said Israel and the PLO would discuss adding international observers from Turkey, Italy, Sweden and Switzerland to the Norwegian force making up the 200-strong Temporary International Presence in Hebron.
In parliament, Netanyahu's coalition handily defeated a motion of no confidence in the government proposed by the far-right Moledet party in protest at the Hebron deal.

But several coalition members, including members of Netanyahu's own cabinet, stayed away during the vote to show they opposed the agreement. Four of Netanyahu's 18 cabinet memebers say they will oppose the deal in a cabinet vote.
